# Python cheat sheet
{font=mono}

![An editor window](<Python cheat sheet.assets/desk.png>)
{width=45%}

Use `python -m venv .venv` to make an environment, then `source .venv/bin/activate`.

## Lists and dicts

```python
squares = [n * n for n in range(10) if n % 2 == 0]
ages = {"ana": 31, "ben": 27}
for name, age in sorted(ages.items()):
    print(f"{name:>6} is {age}")
```

## Reading a file

```python
from pathlib import Path

text = Path("note.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
print(len(text.splitlines()), "lines")
```

## Things to remember

| Need               | Use                       |
|:-------------------|:--------------------------|
| Count things       | `collections.Counter`     |
| Paths              | `pathlib.Path`            |
| Dates              | `datetime`, never strings |
| A default for a key | `dict.get(key, default)` |

- [Never use a list as a default argument.]{color=red}
- ==Prefer f-strings== to `%` and `.format`.
- ~~`os.path.join`~~ is fine, but `Path` reads better.

    An indented block
    is also a code block.

# Sourdough bread

![A finished loaf](<Sourdough bread.assets/bread.jpg>)
{width=70%}

[Makes one loaf. Start the evening before.]{color=gray}

## Ingredients

| Ingredient    | Amount | Note                     |
|:--------------|-------:|:-------------------------|
| Bread flour   |  450 g | [strong]{color=brown}    |
| Whole wheat   |   50 g |                          |
| Water         |  375 g | ==warm, not hot==        |
| Starter       |  100 g | fed 6 hours before       |
| Salt          |   10 g | [add after the rest]{color=red} |

## Method

1. Mix flour and water. Rest **45 minutes**.
2. Add starter and salt. Fold every 30 minutes, ++four times++.
3. Shape, then into the fridge overnight.
   - Seam side up in the basket
   - Cover with a cloth
4. Bake in a covered pot:
   1. 250 °C for 25 minutes, lid on
   2. 220 °C for 20 minutes, lid off

[Let it cool for an hour before cutting.]{bg=yellow}

> The loaf is done when it sounds hollow underneath.

# Welcome
{color=indigo}

This note shows **everything the format can do**. Open it in the editor to see how each line is written.

## Ordinary Markdown

Text can be **bold**, *italic*, ***both***, ~~struck out~~ or `inline code`. A [link](https://example.com) looks like this, and a bare address such as https://example.org becomes a link too.

> A quote sits apart from the text.
> It can run over several lines.

---

## The extras

- Underline: ++this is underlined++
- Highlight: ==this is highlighted==
- Highlight in a colour: [mint background]{bg=mint}
- Text colour by name: [red]{color=red}, [teal]{color=teal}, [purple]{color=purple}
- Text colour by hex: [any colour you like]{color=#c2410c}
- Font: [a serif phrase]{font=serif}, [a mono phrase]{font=mono}, [handwriting]{font="Caveat"}
- Size: [small]{size=small}, [large]{size=large}, [exactly 26px]{size=26px}
- Combined: [**Do not forget this**]{color=white bg=red size=large}
- Styled link: [see [the guide](https://example.com)]{color=green}

This whole paragraph is grey and small because of the line under it.
{color=gray size=small}

## Lists and tasks

1. First step
2. Second step
   - A detail
   - Another detail

- [x] Read this note
- [ ] Make a note of your own

## A table

| Feature   | Written as       | Looks like         |
|:----------|:----------------:|-------------------:|
| Underline | `++text++`       | ++text++           |
| Highlight | `==text==`       | ==text==           |
| Colour    | `[text]{color=blue}` | [text]{color=blue} |

## Code

```js
const greeting = "hello";
console.log(greeting.toUpperCase());
```
